explanation: Encodes Melfi's construction: for every ε > 0 there is an infinite increasing sequence d_i ≥ 2 with Σ 1/(d_i - 1) ≤ ε such that, for every k ≥ 1, all large n are finite sums Σ_{i∈I} a_i with a_i ∈ P(d_i,k). The page states it with P(d_i,0), but with infinitely many bases that version is trivial (n copies of 1 = d_i^0), so moving to k ≠ 0, with that justification, is sensible. I could not check whether [Me04, Prop. 1] gives the 'every k ≠ 0' form exactly.
